{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABi4fbHQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhMO2IE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 152, "title": "Remove automatic recovery save states and simplify state loading", "body": "## Problem

PR #151 added manual save states and an automatic recovery mechanism. In ordinary use, Load can append one or two new full-machine snapshots with random IDs (Recovery · live progress / Recovery · stored progress). Loading an older state repeatedly therefore grows the history without an explicit Save. RTC time/fractional-time changes alone can trigger this, even when the player has not made a new in-game save.

The maintainer has decided to **remove automatic backup/recovery entirely for now**. Do not replace it with capped recovery slots, deduplication, an optional setting, a hidden backup area or another automatic snapshot mechanism. The feature may be reconsidered independently in the future; do not implement compatibility or scaffolding in anticipation of that.

## Expected outcome

- Save-state history grows only when the user explicitly creates a new state (New state + Save) or imports a state. Saving to an existing selected state replaces that state. Load, gameplay, elapsed time, tab visibility changes, Reset and cartridge/model changes never automatically create a save state.
- Load directly validates and restores the selected machine snapshot, including its cartridge save bytes, internal EEPROM and RTC, without creating recovery snapshots or requiring a recovery write. Ordinary game-native persistence follows the restored machine state through the existing save mechanisms.
- Delete the automatic recovery implementation and its dedicated error messages, UI behavior, documentation, tests and otherwise-unused helpers. No backward-compatibility/migration requirement for the removed recovery feature, no compatibility layer or dormant recovery option.
- Keep ordinary manual save-state operations, native SRAM/EEPROM/RTC saving and error handling, ROM/model isolation, safe snapshot validation, existing input/audio/display and visibility behavior.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: [56b5488](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/commit/56b54880b367ddf8837617f7a227b01626d03778), merged PR #151 / Issue #150. Inspect latest main first. This decision supersedes the automatic recovery/backup requirements of #150.

- [web/src/state-restore.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/56b54880b367ddf8837617f7a227b01626d03778/web/src/state-restore.ts#L13-L104): compares live/stored/target native records; creates a new UUID for each recovery snapshot; writes up to two recovery records before applying a state. RTC comparison includes guest clock fractions.
- [web/src/state-picker.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/56b54880b367ddf8837617f7a227b01626d03778/web/src/state-picker.ts#L195-L208): explicit Save correctly reuses selected ID; Load currently reports that previous progress is in the picker when recovery is generated.
- web/src/main.ts: restore callback, restoring guard, heldWrites, periodic native save persistence, visibility and scheduling.
- web/src/saves.ts: recovery-specific inspection, transaction/rollback and cache helpers; preserve preexisting regular save protection and storage failure handling.
- web/src/state-history.ts: normal IndexedDB history and atomic metadata/snapshot writes.
- crates/ws-core and crates/ws-web: audit helpers introduced only for synthesizing recovery snapshots or replacing their native records (e.g. capture_snapshot_at, rtc_data_at, replace_native_records, as applicable). Remove only helpers that have no remaining legitimate callers. Preserve snapshot codec, validation, deterministic continuation and normal RTC rebase.
- web/scripts/save-states.mjs and docs/save-states.md contain dedicated recovery tests and descriptions.

Reproduce with the existing original CC0 RTC fixture: create and select a state, let the clock advance, Load it repeatedly. The current implementation adds Recovery entries although the user has not requested a new state. Repeat with changed cartridge SRAM/EEPROM or internal console EEPROM; Load can also generate recovery entries in those cases.

### Implementation scope

- Remove automatic snapshot generation from the restore path, native-record comparison/recovery branching, recovery-only labels and success/error messages, and recovery-specific write holds/rollback mechanisms if no longer needed. Prefer a straightforward prepare/validate/apply path with existing scheduler protection. Do not keep dead code in case recovery returns later.
- Invalid, malformed, wrong-ROM/model/version or otherwise incompatible snapshots must still be rejected before altering the live machine. Maintain bounded decoding, correct captured-frame redraw, input clearing, host audio flush, RTC anchor rebase, playback intent, visibility behavior and resource cleanup. This task removes automatic preservation of *outgoing* progress, not basic validation or normal error handling.
- Successful Load restores the snapshot's saved native data as part of the machine; ordinary persistence can overwrite the current game's previous SRAM/EEPROM/RTC/console data with the restored data. This is the intended trade-off; document it briefly. No automatic recovery, undo, extra confirmation prompt or backup prerequisite. Users can explicitly Save a separate state first if desired.
- Keep existing normal save storage keys and formats, ROM library and manually created state history where straightforward. No special support for legacy recovery records or old recovery formats, no migration, conversion or compatibility machinery. Do not implement automatic bulk deletion of user-created states or ordinary save data. Previously generated recovery entries need not be migrated or given any special handling; if still present in the generic picker they can be removed using its existing Delete action. No new cleanup UI is required.
- Simplify recovery-related code and tests rather than redesigning the database or snapshot format. Retain the unified picker, New state, selected-state overwrite, explicit Load, Delete, Import/Export and pagination. Remove recovery-only documentation and replace it with the direct-load semantics and warning that older states may replace newer native progress.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Using real Wasm and existing original CC0 fixtures, create a manual state, then repeatedly Load after gameplay, elapsed RTC time and changed native progress. The number and IDs of stored states remain unchanged; no new Recovery entry is created. Successful Load does not need a new IndexedDB write to create a backup.
- [ ] Direct Load restores the expected CPU/frame/device/native data, including SRAM/EEPROM, RTC and internal console EEPROM, without a reset, and the ordinary persistence path subsequently saves the restored values. Verify playing/paused behavior and clock rebase. Wrong/corrupt/incompatible states remain non-destructive.
- [ ] Explicit New state + Save and Import create entries; ordinary Save overwrites the selected entry, with atomic snapshot/thumbnail update; Load, Reset, pause/resume, tab hide/show, cartridge/model changes and ongoing emulation do not create entries. Existing manual picker and ordinary save behavior continue working.
- [ ] Remove automatic recovery-specific implementation, otherwise-unused helpers, UI wording, tests and documentation. Replace obsolete recovery tests with focused direct-load/no-growth regressions rather than merely skipping failing tests. Retain independent snapshot correctness and native persistence checks.
- [ ] Update README/Help and docs/save-states.md to describe direct Load and its effect on newer native progress. Run relevant existing production-preview browser tests (npm ci, npm run build:wasm as needed, npm run build, npm run test:browser, npm run test:compat) and git diff --check. If Rust snapshot/Wasm code changes, run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test --workspace --locked and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; run fixture checks if fixture sources change. Record actual results and limitations.

This is a focused simplification, not a new backup design. Do not expand into migration, cross-tab coordination, compatibility work, extreme viewport testing or a replacement recovery feature. Normal single-tab workflow is supported. No human approval, commercial ROM or physical-device verification is required. Once the requested removal and mandatory tests pass and no material functional defect remains, merge and close.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

After merge and closure, verify the Pages deployment of the merge revision. Smoke-test the published player with an original CC0 RTC or native-save fixture: create a state, advance gameplay/time, Load repeatedly and confirm the history count remains unchanged. Report actual results and limitations. Pending publication checks do not block merge/closure; link confirmed production defects as follow-ups.

outputs.message:
Issue #152 was already closed as completed after PR #153 merged. I posted the verification results on the issue. [Issue comment](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/152#issuecomment-7204796727)

The published GitHub Pages files matched the merge revision’s build artifact byte for byte. In Chromium, three loads of one manual state restored the earlier RTC and SRAM values, and autosave persisted them. The history stayed at one entry with the same state ID after every load. The smoke test used the original CC0 `sram128-2003.ws` fixture. [Pages deployment](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/actions/runs/45905324458)
